source: Dungeons & Dividends rulebook Draft v1, §4 and §8A–8G. Transcribed, not interpreted.
confidenceNote: A house game system. The seven classes are levers that move an FI number, not asset categories and not advice.
note: §7 of the rulebook says 'each of the ten classes' — a leftover from an earlier draft. §4 and the §8A–8G tables both give exactly seven. Seven is authoritative here; see DECISIONS.md DD-003.

asi.note: DD-023. At each ASI level you take +2 to one ability or +1 to two — 5e's rule — or a feat instead. Only INT, WIS and CHA can be raised: they are the abilities you decide, and levelling is exactly when you get to decide again. STR, DEX and CON are measured from money; decreeing +2 income is fiction.

mentorNote: §12B: these are original characters built from schools of thought in FIRE writing, not depictions of real named people.
savesNote: DD-022. Saving-throw proficiencies follow 5e's shape: each class gets one strong save (DEX, CON or WIS) and one weak one (STR, INT or CHA), and every save is covered by at least two classes. The rulebook gave three classes the identical CON/WIS pair and left DEX and INT to one class each; the original pair is kept on each class as savesRulebook.
